title: Flare gas recovery for sustainable energy and hydrogen production: A techno‐economic and multi‐stage simulation study
content:
Abstract

Gas flaring in refinery operations wastes energy and generates substantial greenhouse gas emissions. This study presents an integrated process-simulation and techno-economic assessment of flare gas recovery at the Algiers Refinery (Sidi R'cine, Algeria), comparing two independent valorization pathways modeled in Aspen HYSYS: power generation via a two-stage gas turbine and hydrogen production via steam methane reforming (SMR), shift conversion, and pressure swing adsorption (PSA). For an average flare gas flow of 557.7 kgmol/h (12,500 Nm3/h), the power route, modeled as a complete simple-cycle gas turbine (air compressor, adiabatic combustor at 1281°C and two-stage expansion), delivers 58.7 MW of net power (35.1% LHV efficiency) and displaces grid electricity equivalent to 205,500 tCO2/year, with a total CAPEX of $94.05 M, an NPV of $13.4 M, an IRR of 11.6%, and a discounted payback of 18.5 years. The hydrogen route achieves 83.6% methane conversion and 99.2% cumulative CO conversion; correcting the PSA model to an industrially representative 85% recovery yields 22,232 Nm3/h of high-purity H2 (99.99 mol %) plus 124.2 kgmol/h of LPG co-product, with a complete equipment-by-equipment CAPEX of $51.4 M (2023 USD), an NPV of $334.8 M, an IRR of 52.0%, and a discounted payback of 3.3 years. Evaluated as independent, mutually exclusive scenarios on the same flare gas resource, both routes convert an environmental liability into a viable energy asset, with hydrogen production offering markedly superior financial returns.
